records.people: Ahmed Al Musalmi (Executive President/Governor, Central Bank of Oman, appointed January 2025)
records.move: from chief executive of Sohar International Bank (since 2018) to Executive President of the Central Bank of Oman
records.summary: The National reports that Al Musalmi was appointed governor of Oman's central bank, replacing Tahir Al Amri, and that he was at the time chief executive of Sohar International Bank, a role held since 2018. The appointment page does not state the bank's ownership; a separate shareholding breakdown for Sohar International Bank SAOG lists mixed ownership - State or Government 11.6 percent (Royal Court Affairs 11.6 percent, Oman Investment Authority 4.53 percent), Private Companies 17.3 percent, Public Companies 11 percent, Institutions 15.6 percent and General Public 44.5 percent (https://simplywall.st/stocks/om/banks/msm-bksb/sohar-international-bank-saog-shares/ownership). Head-office city is not stated on either page, so it is left null.
records.source_title: Oman appoints new central bank governor (The National)
records.quote: Mr Al Musalmi is currently the chief executive of Oman's Sohar International Bank.

records.people: Maksat Ishenbaev (Deputy Chairman of the board, National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, until 2007)
records.move: from Deputy Chairman of the board of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic (until 2007) to chairman of the board of MBANK (OJSC Commercial Bank Kyrgyzstan), taking office 15 January 2025
records.summary: Kaktus.media gives a dated career: he headed Energo Bank 2000-2004; was deputy chairman of the National Bank board until 2007; headed the representative office of OJSC Bank CenterCredit 2007-2010; was chairman of the board of Zalkar Bank 2010-2012; then headed a leasing company and an insurance company; became chairman of the board of Bai-Tushum bank in December 2017; chairman of the supervisory board of the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange in May 2018; and took office as chairman of the board of MBANK on 15 January 2025. The page states no ownership for any employer. MBANK's audited accounts filed with the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange state its shareholders as a private individual, O. T. Babanov, holding 97.97 percent at 31 December 2024 (A. T. Babanova held the same stake at 31 December 2023), with 2.03 percent held by other physical and legal persons and no state body listed (https://www.kse.kg/Listing/KAKB-auditreport-2025-06-20.pdf). Head-office city is not stated on either page, so it is left null. Ownership of Energo Bank, Bank CenterCredit, Zalkar Bank and Bai-Tushum is not stated by any page opened.
records.quote: До 2007 года занимал должность заместителя председателя правления НБ КР.

records.people: Safwat Raslan (Governor of the Central Bank of Syria, appointed May 2026)
records.move: from branch manager at Byblos Bank Syria, banking expert at TARGOBANK and Deutsche Bank and credit business manager at Deutsche Apotheker und Aerztebank, via director general of the Syrian Development Fund, to Governor of the Central Bank of Syria
records.summary: Enab Baladi reports that Raslan was a credit business manager at Deutsche Apotheker und Aerztebank in Germany, worked as a consultant at EY and Capco, as a banking expert at TARGOBANK and Deutsche Bank, and as a branch manager at Byblos Bank Syria, and that his most recent position was director general of the Syrian Development Fund. The page gives no dates and states no ownership for any employer. A BLOMINVEST Bank sector review lists the bank he worked at, under the entry "Shahba Bank (Previously Bank Byblos)", in a table titled "Syria's private and foreign banking sector: Q3 2024" (https://blog.blominvestbank.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/A-Look-at-Syria%E2%80%99s-Banking-Sector.pdf); ownership of TARGOBANK, Deutsche Bank and Deutsche Apotheker und Aerztebank is not stated on any page opened, so they are not filed as settled parties. No head-office city is stated anywhere, so it is left null; only the country Germany is stated, for Deutsche Apotheker und Aerztebank.
records.source_title: Sharaa Appoints Safwat Raslan Central Bank Governor (Enab Baladi)
records.quote: He served as a credit business manager at Deutsche Apotheker und Ärztebank in Germany.

records.people: Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani (Governor, Qatar Central Bank)
records.move: from Head of the State Audit Bureau (2015-2021) to Governor of the Qatar Central Bank
records.summary: The Gulf Monetary Council board page gives his career entirely inside public bodies: an early Qatar Central Bank career in the Credit and Banking Supervision Section and then the Investment Department as head of trading and managing the foreign exchange reserves; a role establishing and then leading the Qatar Credit Bureau as CEO, with the Banking Risk Department added in 2014; Head of the State Audit Bureau 2015-2021; and Governor of the Qatar Central Bank. The page names no bank, asset manager or other private financial firm, so this is recorded as a move between public bodies.
records.source_title: H.E. Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani (Gulf Monetary Council, Board of Directors)
records.quote: Prior to this appointment, he was Head of the State Audit Bureau during the period 2015-2021.

records.people: Dasho Penjore (Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan from December 2015; Deputy Managing Director 2003-2006)
records.move: from Chief Executive Officer of the National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan to Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (December 2015)
records.summary: The Financial Institutions Training Institute board page states he started his career at the Royal Monetary Authority in 1987, served as Deputy Managing Director 2003-2006, was appointed Chief Chamberlain to the King in 2006, and was Chief Executive Officer of the National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan before being appointed Governor in December 2015. The National Pension & Provident Fund is a statutory pension body, so the only outside employers named are public; the page names no commercial bank or private financial firm.

records.quote: Before he was appointed as the Governor, he was the Chief Executive Officer of National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan.

records.people: Tatafu Moeaki (Governor of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga; director of the National Reserve Bank Board 2013-2016)
records.move: from Minister for Finance of Tonga (until 10 August 2022), and earlier Tonga country head of the Asian Development Bank and World Bank liaison, to Governor of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga
records.summary: Loop Tonga reports his appointment as Governor on 20 December following an open recruitment process, on the recommendation of the Finance Minister in consultation with the Reserve Bank Board. It gives a career wholly in public bodies: director of the National Reserve Bank Board 2013-2016, during which he was also the Government's chief economic adviser and CEO of the Ministry of Finance; former CEO of the Ministry of Trade and Economic Development; World Bank liaison; Asian Development Bank Tonga country head; Member of Parliament and Minister for Finance until 10 August 2022. No commercial bank or private financial firm is named.
records.source_title: Tonga appoints new reserve bank governor (Loop Tonga)
records.quote: Moeaki has had a civil service distinguished career in finance and economic development.

records.people: Naji Mohamed Issa Belqasem (Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Libya from 2005; Governor from October 2024)
records.move: from Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Libya to work as a private economic consultant for international institutions, most notably the International Monetary Fund, then senior advisor to the Minister of Finance from 2018, and back to the Central Bank of Libya as Governor in October 2024
records.summary: Wikipedia states he was appointed Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Libya in 2005, served after 2011 as a private economic consultant for multiple international institutions, most notably the International Monetary Fund, re-entered public service in 2018 as senior advisor to the Minister of Finance, and was appointed Governor in September 2024 and installed on 3 October 2024, with the House of Representatives accepting his resignation on 22 October 2026. The consultancy was his own practice and the only client named is the IMF, so the outside employers named are public; no bank, asset manager or other private financial firm is named. Recorded from Wikipedia only, as a last resort.
